Spatially Link SUS Data to Brazilian Geographic Units

Source: R/sus_join_spatial.R
sus_spatial_join.Rd

Joins a standardized SUS climasus_df to official Brazilian geographic boundaries (municipality, health region, biome, census-related and environmental layers, neighborhoods) or geocodes postal codes (CEP), and returns an sf object. Run it after sus_data_standardize() (stage "stand" or later, e.g. after filtering/derivation/aggregation steps) and before sus_census_join() / the sus_grid_*() + sus_grid_join() steps and the spatial models (sus_mod_spatial_*()). It works for all DATASUS systems with a municipality column (SIM, SIH, SINAN, SIA, CNES, SINASC); level = "cep" needs SIH or CNES, "health_facilities" needs CNES and "neighborhood" needs CNES or SIH.

Usage

sus_spatial_join(
  df,
  level = "munic",
  join_col = NULL,
  lang = "pt",
  use_cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df (non-climasus_df input, including a plain data.frame, errors) whose sus_meta stage is "stand" or later, with at least one row. It needs a geographic identifier column (see join_col); a date column is expected when the result is stored in the metadata. Created by sus_data_import() -> sus_data_clean_encoding() -> sus_data_standardize() (optionally followed by filtering/aggregation).

level

Character scalar. Geographic unit to join; default "munic". Invalid values error. Options:

  • Administrative: "munic" (municipality polygons, default).

  • Health: "health_region", "health_facilities" (CNES only, joined by CNES code), "schools".

  • Environmental: "amazon", "biomes", "conservation_units", "disaster_risk_area", "semiarid", "indigenous_land".

  • Urban: "neighborhood" (SIH or CNES), "urban_area", "metro_area", "urban_concentrations", "pop_arrangements".

  • Postal code: "cep" (SIH or CNES only; geocoded to POINTs with geocodebr).

Except for "cep", "health_facilities" and "neighborhood", the link is made through the municipality code; municipality codes of 6 or 7 digits are matched against the 6-digit IBGE code. Rows with no match in the boundary layer are dropped (inner join) and rows can be repeated when a municipality falls in several units (many-to-many).

join_col

Character scalar naming the column of df that holds the geographic identifier (municipality code, or CEP for level = "cep"). NULL (default) auto-detects: for "munic" the first present of codigo_municipio_ocorrencia, codigo_municipio_residencia, codigo_municipio, codigo_municipio_nascimento, codigo_municipio_paciente, uf_municipio_estabelecimento, CODMUNRES (and their English/Spanish equivalents) in that priority; for "cep" the CEP/zip-code column. A name not in df errors; if auto-detection fails an error lists the expected columns. The column is coerced to character (CEPs are zero-padded to 8 digits) and renamed to code_muni (or cep) in the result.

lang

Character scalar. Message language: "pt" (default), "en" or "es"; other values fall back to "pt" with a warning.

use_cache

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), boundary layers are cached on disk in cache_dir (Parquet/GeoPackage) and reused; FALSE downloads them again.

cache_dir

Character scalar. Directory for the cache; created if missing. Default "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial".

verbose

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), prints progress, cache status and join statistics.

Value

An sf object that is also a climasus_df: all columns of df plus the attributes of the joined layer and a geometry column (POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON for areal levels, POINT for "cep" and "health_facilities"). For level = "munic" it adds code_muni (6 digits), code_muni_7 (7 digits), name_muni, etc. sus_meta is updated to stage = "spatial", type = <level>, spatial = TRUE; the system is preserved and a history entry is appended.

Details

Caching: boundary layers are downloaded once (via geobr and related sources) and cached in cache_dir, which makes repeated calls much faster and allows offline reuse.

Code normalization: all join columns become character; 7-digit municipality codes are matched on their first 6 digits; CEPs are left-padded with zeros to 8 characters.

References

Pereira, R.H.M.; Goncalves, C.N.; et. all (2019) geobr: Loads Shapefiles of Official Spatial Data Sets of Brazil. GitHub repository - https://github.com/ipeaGIT/geobr. Pereira, Rafael H. M.; Barbosa, Rogerio J. (2023) censobr: Download Data from Brazil's Population Census. R package version v0.4.0, https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=censobr. DOI: 10.32614/CRAN.package.censobr.

See also

sus_data_standardize(), sus_data_aggregate(), sus_census_join(), sus_grid_join(), sus_data_plot_aggregate_map()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(climasus4r)

# Example 1: link mortality data to municipalities
df_sim <- sus_data_import(uf = "SP", year = 2023, system = "SIM-DO") |>
  sus_data_standardize(lang = "pt")

sf_sim <- sus_spatial_join(df = df_sim, level = "munic", lang = "pt")

# Example 2: geocode CEP for hospitalization data (SIH/CNES only)
df_sih <- sus_data_import(uf = "RJ", year = 2023, system = "SIH-RD") |>
  sus_data_standardize(lang = "pt")

sf_cep <- sus_spatial_join(df = df_sih, level = "cep", lang = "pt")

# Example 3: link to health regions, naming the municipality column
sf_reg <- sus_spatial_join(
  df       = df_sim,
  level    = "health_region",
  join_col = "codigo_municipio_residencia"
)
} # }
